headline: AI adoption backfire: companies scrambling to fix worker errors and quality problems

bullets.title: Companies rushing into AI are now cleaning up the mess
bullets.summary: Meta and other firms that rapidly deployed AI tools are discovering workers are spending time fixing low-quality output and errors instead of doing their actual jobs. The speed of adoption outpaced the ability to manage real workplace fallout.

bullets.title: Graduates gaming job applications with AI, but say they have no choice
bullets.summary: Young people are increasingly using AI to misrepresent themselves on job applications—inflating skills they don't have or exaggerating experience. Researchers say applicants feel pressured into the practice because competition is so fierce.

bullets.title: Factory robots that can switch tasks in minutes, not weeks—more jobs at risk
bullets.summary: A startup called Industrial Next is making robots flexible enough to handle complex, delicate work that has traditionally required human labor, and switch between different tasks much faster than before. This technology could accelerate automation across manufacturing.

headline: AI is outpacing workplace safety rules, while Amazon's robot army raises questions about human jobs

bullets.title: Microsoft president warns AI is less regulated than milk
bullets.summary: Microsoft's Brad Smith is calling for urgent government oversight of AI systems, saying the technology has fewer safety rules than household products. The warning comes as AI companies face growing pressure to put guardrails in place before the technology disrupts more industries.

bullets.title: Amazon now has over 1 million robot workers—here's what it means for humans
bullets.summary: The second-largest U.S. employer has doubled down on automation, deploying robots across warehouses and fulfillment centers. The shift raises hard questions about what happens to the hundreds of thousands of human workers who currently do those jobs.

bullets.title: IMF warns AI is a 'slow-moving tsunami' hitting young workers hardest
bullets.summary: International Monetary Fund leaders say artificial intelligence is reshaping the global job market, with the youngest workers facing the steepest exposure to AI-driven displacement. The World Bank is now urging governments to adopt emergency-level employment support measures.

bullets.title: Fired OpenAI researchers claim they were let go for pushing safety concerns
bullets.summary: Several researchers at OpenAI say the company terminated them for prioritizing AI safety over commercial speed, though OpenAI disputes this and claims they mishandled sensitive information. The clash highlights growing tension between safety advocates and AI companies racing to deploy new systems.
